failure_patterns.pattern: cached_followup_action_omission: Newly supplied criteria or pending trip details were ignored or only cached results were retrieved, without applying the requested search or filter.

rejected_edits.content: When the assistant asks for missing travel dates for an already-requested itinerary, a user's stated preferred or ideal travel date answers that request; assign it only to the requested leg or domain it answers (for example, as a flight departure date, or as hotel check-in when the user also gives a stay duration). For a requested round trip, use an explicitly stated return date as the return-leg departure date; use it as hotel checkout only when it is the stated end of the hotel stay. Continue using `adjust_date` for a known hotel duration in nights. Do not treat an event date as a travel date or infer unrequested domains or legs.
rejected_edits.target: Associate dates with explicitly stated itinerary legs in the order and context given, and do not ask again for dates already supplied.

rejected_edits.content: For time-range fields, use the schema's accepted clock notation (for example, `08:23 PM`), not 24-hour values with seconds unless the schema requires them. Encode an exact time as `[time, time]`; encode “by” or “until” a time as `[12:00 AM, time]`, and “at or after” a time as `[time, 11:59 PM]`.
rejected_edits.target: For range-shaped fields, encode an explicitly exact value as both endpoints (for example, `[n, n]`); encode a minimum rating or a request for at least or better as `[n, schema_max]`.
